items.headline: U.S. Stocks Show Mixed Performance, Boosted by AI Optimism and Earnings
items.summary: U.S. equities closed a mixed session today, October 21, 2026, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average advancing significantly, while the S&P 500 saw modest gains and the Nasdaq Composite edged lower. Positive earnings from key AI-related companies, notably SpaceX and Super Micro Computer, bolstered market sentiment, offsetting concerns related to rising oil prices and disappointing reports from some consumer-facing companies.

items.headline: Super Micro Computer Jumps on Upgraded Revenue Outlook
items.summary: Shares of Super Micro Computer ($SMCI) surged over 10% today, closing at $36.02, up +$3.55 (+10.93%), after the company significantly raised its preliminary Q1 FY2027 revenue outlook to between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion from an earlier forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. This substantial increase was attributed to robust demand for its AI platforms.

items.headline: SpaceX Climbs on Strong Q3 Earnings, AI Business Growth
items.summary: SpaceX ($SPCX) shares advanced over 11% today after the company reported stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings and revenue. The rocket launch and satellite communications firm saw its revenue climb to $14.6 billion, a 161% year-over-year increase, driven largely by its Super Intelligence artificial intelligence segment, which surged 830% year-over-year.

items.headline: Capital One Financial Rises on Positive Earnings Report
items.summary: Capital One Financial ($COF) saw its stock price increase by +4.11%, reaching $209.84, as it rallied on profit reports that topped analysts' expectations, contributing to overall market strength.

items.headline: Netflix Shares Decline Post-Earnings on Ad Revenue Cut
items.summary: Netflix ($NFLX) shares fell about 6% after hours, following its earnings report. While the company's EPS of $0.87 beat estimates and revenue of $12.87 billion was in line, investors reacted negatively to a cut in its 2026 ad revenue forecast from $3 billion to approximately $2.7 billion, indicating the slowest growth in three years.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary and Tech Lead, Utilities and Real Estate Lag
items.summary: Today's market saw the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) lead gains, rising by 1.8% and 1.4% respectively, driven by renewed AI optimism. Conversely, the Utilities Select Sector SPDR (XLU) and Real Estate Select Sector SPDR (XLRE) were among the weakest performers, falling 2% and 1.2% respectively, as eight out of eleven sectors of the broad market index ended in negative territory.

items.headline: Fed's Next Rate Decision Looms as Inflation Remains Elevated
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision is scheduled for October 27 and 28, with market participants anticipating a potential rate hike by year-end. Minutes from the September meeting indicated most officials believe another increase in the federal funds rate target range would likely be appropriate. Consumer prices for the 12 months ending in September rose to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August, maintaining pressure on the Fed to address elevated inflation.

items.headline: Homebuilder Sentiment and Pending Home Sales Hit Lows
items.summary: Economic data released today highlighted significant weakness in the housing sector. Homebuilder sentiment dropped to its lowest level since 2012, while U.S. pending home sales in September fell 7.3%, significantly missing expectations and reaching a record low. This indicates elevated borrowing costs are weighing heavily on the interest-rate-sensitive housing market.

items.headline: Tesla and Meta Platforms Awaited Post-Market Earnings
items.summary: Investors are closely watching for after-market earnings reports from tech giants Tesla ($TSLA) and Meta Platforms ($META) today. Tesla's results will follow news that both its board and SpaceX's board have formed independent special committees to review a possible merger, a development Elon Musk noted is not yet a finalized deal.

items.headline: Oil Prices Fluctuate Amid Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Oil prices showed mixed signals today, with Brent crude closing near $110 a barrel amid reports of attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz, suggesting ongoing geopolitical tensions. However, other reports indicated WTI crude fell 1.8% to about $102 on hopes of U.S.-Iran diplomacy, creating conflicting pressures on energy markets.
